source_evidence.finding: Calendar-list request has no query parameters or continuation loop; decoded list has no nextPageToken. Google documentation defaults hidden entries off and paginates lists. This disproves a universal completeness promise, not a demonstrated production incident.

excerpts.text:
struct GoogleCalendarListResponse: Codable {
    let kind: String
    let etag: String
    let items: [GoogleCalendarItem]
}

struct GoogleCalendarItem: Codable {
    let kind: String
    let etag: String
    let id: String
    let summary: String
    let timeZone: String?
    let colorId: String?
    let backgroundColor: String?
    let foregroundColor: String?
}

source_evidence.finding: Downloads depend on selected mirrored calendar IDs; mirror source can be local, first CalDAV, or default-calendar source. Download request bounds are now minus180/plus360days; no promise that every historical event is available.
Inspected Google event serialization supplies attendees and event fields, not Google guest permission flags. Bounded finding: no equivalent control claimed for Cloud UI.
Google calendars grouped under stored user and selection toggle; specific provider calendar mapping used for sharing.
Native text distinguishes Reader viewing/sync, Writer editing, Owner sharing/access using invited email.
Import records signed-in or anonymous received invitation; record failure caught separately. Receipt is not an attendance response.
Generated feeds may be scoped to one event or whole calendar; do not conflate with Google secret address.
Feed retrieval GET and cache-control do not prove receiver fetch/display timing.
METHOD:PUBLISH with PT1H refresh/TTL hints; no guaranteed refresh deadline.
Owner-only feed grant revocation deletes feed/index; not evidence erasing remote independent copies.
Original three thin guides contain unsupported universal exposure/no-record/default/complete-calendar claims; drafts replace only these canonical objects. Exact lines depend on this hashed snapshot.
